title: DeBiasMe: De-biasing Human-AI Interactions with Metacognitive AIED (AI in Education) Interventions
venue: Proceedings of Workshop: AI Augmented Reasoning (CHI ’25)
extended_summary:
This position paper addresses a gap in AI literacy and human-AI interaction research: how to reduce human cognitive biases such as anchoring, confirmation bias, and automation bias when learners use generative AI tools. The author argues that current AI literacy approaches focus too heavily on technical prompting and on algorithmic/systemic bias, while paying too little attention to the human side of the interaction, especially metacognition and self-regulation.

The paper proposes DeBiasMe, a metacognitive AI in education intervention intended to support bias awareness and critical engagement with AI. The design is built around deliberate friction, bi-directional intervention across both prompt formulation and output interpretation, and adaptive scaffolding for different user needs. Two illustrative components are described: a prompt refinement tool that flags potentially biased prompts before submission, and a bias visualization map that helps users inspect AI outputs for different kinds of bias and their relationships.

The context discussed is higher education, based on a mixed-methods user study with university students using surveys and interviews to identify metacognitive support needs. However, the paper is primarily a conceptual and design-oriented position paper rather than a full evaluation study. Its main conclusion is that bias-aware AI literacy should move beyond operational prompt skills toward metacognitive support that helps students monitor their own reasoning, recognize bias interactions, and use AI more critically and intentionally.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper with conceptual framing and design proposals, not a controlled empirical study. It includes references to prior and ongoing work, but the paper itself does not report a clear experimental or quasi-experimental methodology or outcome estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The proposed intervention has plausible educational value for metacognition and responsible AI use, but the paper provides no measured effect sizes or demonstrated population-level impact. As a result, impact remains promising but unclear based on this paper alone.

interventions.use_case: Metacognitive AI literacy intervention (DeBiasMe) that adds deliberate friction to human-AI workflows via prompt refinement feedback and post-response bias visualization to help students detect and mitigate cognitive biases when using GenAI/LLMs.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that the DeBiasMe prototype and its prior user research support improvements in metacognitive knowledge and regulation, helping students become more aware of their own reasoning and bias patterns during AI use. The paper reports that earlier prototype evaluation using usability heuristics, think-aloud studies, and expert reviews suggested the tool made implicit human and AI biases explicit and actionable, but it does not provide controlled effect sizes or inferential statistics.
finding.measure: Metacognitive awareness/regulation, critical thinking during AI interaction; usability heuristics, think-aloud studies, expert reviews, and mixed-method user research

finding.finding_summary: The paper positions DeBiasMe as a bridge between academic integrity policies and students’ everyday GenAI use, with the goal of supporting responsible AI governance in educational settings. This is a conceptual and design-oriented claim rather than an outcome evaluation, so no effect size or sample-based impact estimate is reported.
finding.measure: Policy and governance relevance for academic integrity and responsible AI use
